paragraphs.text: WUBRG (/wu'bɜːɹg/, from the phonetic transcription of the mana symbols ) is a term used for one of each colored mana; white , blue , black , red , and green .
The philosophy of WUBRG is about the necessity of understanding all the different philosophies of the various colors. The true path of life is finding the intersection of all five.
There are only a few cards with mana cost . Most of them are legendary like the Child of Alara , legendary Slivers and characters like Niv-Mizzet in his function as the Living Guildpact .
Who/What/When/Where/Why is a five-color instant card but only has one color when cast.
Transguild Courier and Sphinx of the Guildpact are five-colored cards but cost generic mana to play. Fallaji Wayfarer has a similar ability, but its mana cost also includes green mana.
Awaken the Maelstrom and O-Kagachi Made Manifest are the back faces of cards that cost to cast and are themselves five-colored.

With the rise of Commander and its color identity rules, a newer design is to slot in all five symbols in the text box in a way that doesn't affect its casting cost too much. Golos, Tireless Pilgrim is infamous for being a Commander that can be cast off colorless sources such as Sol Ring and finds colors off lands like the Triomes , potentially resulting in a deck of only the best spells in every color and no real theming. In order contexts, there are things like Morophon, the Boundless , a generically typal commander that can be used for any subtype without a proper Legendary creature to helm the deck. Alternatively, the subtype is spread somewhat evenly across three or more colors, but the deck's strategy would not want to expend resources fixing its mana, and so putting it in the text box gets around that issue.
paragraphs.section: Cards with WUBRG in their text box

paragraphs.text: Some cards can add either by directly having the five mana symbols in the text box like Crystal Quarry or by referencing it through text like Leyline Immersion . Even rarer is the ability to add in addition like Opening Ceremony .
Krosa is a Plane that can add when chaos ensues .
Morophon, the Boundless can reduce the cost of other spells by , but only colored mana. Aang, Master of Elements has the same ability but can also reduce generic mana .
paragraphs.section: Cards that reduce costs by WUBRG

paragraphs.text: Some cards like Golos, Tireless Pilgrim require to activate an ability .

Some have multiple abilities which require to activate them all. Examples are Kenrith, the Returned King which has as one ability for each color or Cromat which as one ability of each enemy color pairing.

The Bringer cycle from Fifth Dawn allows you to pay to cast them instead of their considerably higher mana costs. Cards Fist of Suns and Jodah, Archmage Eternal allow you to pay instead of any spell's mana cost in general. Etched Oracle Avatar is a Magic Online Vanguard with the same effect.
Some special promotional , playtest , and other special printings feature mana in some capacity:
1996 World Champion is the first card printed with cost and only one copy of this card exists.
Slivdrazi Monstrosity is a playtest card that first used mana.
The following Heroes of the Realm cards use in either cost or text box: Wizard from Beyond ; Ersta, Friend to All ; Nira, Hellkite Duelist ; Fabled Path of Searo Point ; Andrios, Roaming Explorer .
Some My Little Pony crossover cards use in the text box: Princess Twilight Sparkle & Rainbow Dash .
